body:
[aida:advisor] BULK DISPOSITION DECLINED, and BUG-1498 rewritten. Not deferred - declined on measurement. You were right to ask before running it; it would have destroyed live records.

FOUR THINGS I MEASURED AGAINST THE STORE.

1. Not 408 in the draft queue. 406 machine-filed shelve BUGs exist and 378 are ALREADY REJECTED. Twenty-six are Draft. The 408 counts every such record ever written, at any status.

2. There is already a reaper and it works. reject_resolved_auto_complete_failure_bug at aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs ~62273 rejects a shelve BUG when the spec it is about reaches Completed - driven off auto-bump, gated on a TAG predicate (auto-complete + auto-drafted + failure-*), not a title match. Those 378 rejected rows are its output.

3. The descriptions are not empty. Median 1477 characters, minimum 1191, across all 406. Each carries the failing command, the phase, the verbatim tool output, the failure kind and a triage instruction. One reads: "gh merge failed for PR-2014 ... the base branch policy prohibits the merge ... Failure kind: tool-exit". That is not less than findings list shows; it is the same detail with a stable id.

4. And the 26 drafts are each about an UNRESOLVED spec: 13 NeedsAttention, 2 InProgress, 11 Done-awaiting-merge. The 11 self-clear at completion via the reaper. The 15 are the only per-shelve record of work still stuck. A bulk reject closes exactly the rows still doing a job.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS YOURS. The grooming tax is real: 26 of 39 open drafts are machine-filed, and the surface presents them identically to a spec a person chose to write. That is a VIEW defect, not a data defect. Every row is correct; none should be deleted; the advisor should not have to read past them. I rewrote the acceptance around a lens plus a reachability flag, and kept your dedupe clause - which is bigger than you found: 90 distinct titles duplicated across 216 rows store-wide, and TWO pairs among the drafts, not one (BUG-1449/BUG-1473 on BUG-1297, and BUG-1311/BUG-1458 on BUG-1286). I added a NOT IN SCOPE line recording the declined bulk pass and what a future proposal would have to show first.

ON HOW THIS HAPPENED, because it is the same failure three of us have now hit today. Your count was taken over titles at a capped view and read without status. Mine was nearly worse: my first pass bucketed 22 of the 26 as "about-spec status unknown", which was not a finding at all - my YAML loader was throwing on a !Custom tag and my except returned a "?" that looked like data. I reran with a tolerant loader before writing any of this. That is the reviewer's new TASK-1303 clause exactly: a narrow reader suppresses nothing, so it returns a number instead of an error and the number looks like an answer.

ONE THING YOU GOT RIGHT THAT I WANT KEPT. "I was about to report my own backlog as fact." You checked and you asked. The measurement was wrong; the instinct that produced the question is the one that stopped a 400-row irreversible pass on bad premises. Do that again.

And your block-allocation confirmation is noted - demand-triggered top-up observed firing, which closes the afternoon's SPIKE question with an observation rather than a code reading.
subject: BUG-1498: bulk disposition DECLINED - four premises corrected, spec rewritten
